description: A single-panel CALPHAD property diagram (Thermo-Calc style, identified as Fig. 10) whose x-axis is "Temperature [K]" with labelled ticks at 600, 900, 1200 and 1500 K and whose y-axis is "Amount of all phases [mol]" from 0.0 to 1.2 in 0.2 increments. Six colour-coded curves are defined by the legend: B2_VACANCY(AL:NI) (dark blue), BCC_A2(FE:MN:VA) (red), BCC_A2#2(MN:VA,C) (green), LIQUID(FE:MN) (purple), M3SI(MN:FE:SI) (olive) and BCC_A2#3(FE:VA) (orange). Red BCC_A2 dominates: it rises steeply to about 0.6 by ~600 K, plateaus near 0.7-0.75 up to ~1100 K, and collapses steeply to zero at ~1500 K. Dark-blue B2 is ~0.3 at 500 K and decreases monotonically to zero at ~1500 K. Purple Liquid is zero until ~1100 K, then climbs steeply, dipping near 1400 K and reaching ~1.0 at 1500 K. Orange BCC_A2#3 and olive M3Si vanish below ~600 K and ~800 K; green BCC_A2#2 stays near zero with a small step near 1100 K. Arrow annotations name BCC_A2, B2, Liquid, BCC_A2#2, BCC_A2#3 and M3Si directly on the curves. A tiny ternary triangle schematic occupies the lower-left corner. Together the panel shows the equilibrium phase evolution with temperature for one composition.

observations.observation: The y-axis is labelled 'Amount of all phases [mol]' and spans 0.0 to 1.2 with gridline ticks every 0.2 mol.
The x-axis is labelled 'Temperature [K]' with printed ticks at 600, 900, 1200 and 1500 K; the plotted range begins near 500 K.
The legend lists six phases: B2_VACANCY(AL:NI), BCC_A2(FE:MN:VA), BCC_A2#2(MN:VA,C), LIQUID(FE:MN), M3SI(MN:FE:SI) and BCC_A2#3(FE:VA).
The red BCC_A2 curve is the largest fraction over most of the range: it rises steeply to about 0.6 by ~600 K, then plateaus near 0.7-0.75 between 900 and 1100 K before falling to zero at ~1500 K.
The dark-blue B2 (B2_VACANCY(AL:NI)) curve starts at about 0.3 at the low-temperature end and decreases monotonically to zero at ~1500 K.
The purple LIQUID(FE:MN) curve is zero up to about 1100 K, then rises steeply, shows a local dip near 1400 K and reaches about 1.0 mol at 1500 K.
The red BCC_A2 and purple Liquid curves cross in the vicinity of ~1350-1400 K, marking the temperature above which liquid becomes the dominant phase.
The orange BCC_A2#3 curve falls from about 0.45 at 500 K to zero at ~600 K, and the olive M3SI curve falls from about 0.15 to zero at ~800 K.
The green BCC_A2#2 curve stays near zero (a few hundredths of a mole) across the whole range, with a small step increase at roughly 1100 K.
Phase names are annotated directly on the curves with arrows: BCC_A2, B2, Liquid, BCC_A2#2, BCC_A2#3 and M3Si; no numeric data labels are printed on any curve.
A small ternary triangle schematic is drawn at the bottom-left corner, outside the axes; its labels are illegible.

The caption states the calculation used the TCFE8 database for the Fe.Mn.Ni.Al.Si.C system at pressure 100000.0 Pa and system size 1.0 mol, with mole fraction Mn = 0.19, Ni = 0.15, Al = 0.15, Si = 0.1, C = 0.01.
The caption identifies the figure as a 'Property diagram of high entropy steel through CALPHAD modelling' (Fig. 10).
The study is on a low-density high entropy steel of nominal composition Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 processed by mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering.
